The Taylor number is to be calculated for a rotating inner cylinder and stationary outer cylinder.
Use an inner radius of 5 cm (0.05 m).
Use an outer radius of 5.2 cm (0.052 m), giving a gap of 2 mm (0.002 m).
Use an inner cylinder rotational speed of 100 rpm, giving an angular velocity of 10.472 rad/s.
Use a fluid dynamic viscosity of 0.01 Pa·s.
Assume a fluid density of 1000 kg/m³, since density is not given in the original problem.
Calculate kinematic viscosity as dynamic viscosity divided by density, giving 1×10⁻⁵ m²/s.
Calculate the Taylor number using Ta = Ω² r_i (r_o - r_i)³ / ν².
Use r_i = 0.05 m, r_o - r_i = 0.002 m, Ω = 10.472 rad/s, and ν = 1×10⁻⁵ m²/s.
The resulting Taylor number is approximately 438.6, which rounds to 439.
Note that the density of 1000 kg/m³ is an assumption and not part of the original problem statement.
